title: unified-rollouts-canary-shadow-autorollback-enhancements
author: Elliot Chen
release_notes:
- Enhanced unified rollouts: improved canary + shadow integration with automatic rollback triggers.
- Added composite metric thresholds and quarantine stage to reduce false positives.
- New observability metrics and console views for rollback reasoning.
- Backward-compatible API changes; no client migration required.
description:
Motivation: stabilize canary + shadow + A/B rollout workflows and reduce noise-driven rollbacks. Customers saw oscillating rollouts where transient latency spikes caused full rollbacks; this PR introduces a quarantine probing stage, composite metric quorum, and better telemetry to make autorollback decisions more robust.

Summary of changes: added a new rollout state 'quarantine' between probing and fail that requires metric quorum across multiple dimensions before triggering a rollback; extended the autorollback engine to support composite metrics (weighted combination of latency, error-rate, and quality regressions); added a staged probing policy that runs short traffic probes under shadow for 2 minutes before promoting canary traffic; introduce configurable hysteresis windows and jitter to prevent thundering re-evaluations; surface detailed rollback reason and metric snapshots in the Console; add e2e tests and chaos tests for stability.

Design notes: the quarantine stage runs lightweight, targeted probes (small batch of requests using representative prompt shards) and requires at least 2 of 3 metric guards to exceed thresholds for quarantine to escalate to rollback. The composite metric is computed server-side by combining z-normalized signals; thresholds are configurable per-rollout. Hysteresis and minimum evaluation windows ensure transient blips do not immediately flip state.

Compatibility and migration: rollout API remains backward compatible. New fields (quarantine_policy, composite_metrics, quorum) are optional and default to previous behavior, so existing rollouts are unaffected. Admins can opt-in per rollout via the Console or API.

Testing and validation: unit tests for the autorollback decision tree; deterministic integration tests for canary-promote/quarantine/rollback paths; new e2e stability test that injects latency spikes and verifies no unnecessary rollback within configured hysteresis. Ran internal canary on redwood-internal stack for 48 hours with a synthetic traffic pattern; behavior matched expectations and prevented two previously observed false-positive rollbacks.

Rollout plan: merge to main, enable feature flag rollout.quarantine for 25% of internal accounts, monitor for 72 hours with new telemetry dashboards, then progressively increase to 100% unless manual rollback is requested. Readiness gates include: baseline composite_metric false-positive rate < 0.5% and no increase in user-visible 95th latency beyond configured SLO.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of quarantine stage and composite metrics in rollout engine
- [x] Console UI updates to show quarantine state and metric snapshots
- [x] Config schema changes with defaults
- [x] Unit + integration + e2e tests
- [x] Internal canary validation and metrics dashboards
- [x] Documentation updates (api/rollouts.md)

Notes: this PR touches core runtime decision paths; be conservative with changes and rely on feature flags. Followup work: expose a metric-level tuning UI on Console and add per-customer default profiles (latency-sensitive, quality-sensitive).
